name: php_post_password_loose_eq
reason: Loose == against $_POST lets password=0 or password=true bypass a non-empty stored password.

name: php_get_role_loose_ne
reason: Loose != against $_GET can be tricked by type coercion, e.g. an array or boolean role value.

name: php_request_token_loose_eq
reason: $_REQUEST is attacker-controlled the same way as $_GET/$_POST; loose == is bypassable.

name: php_cookie_session_loose_eq
reason: A cookie value compared loosely to 1 can be satisfied by "1abc" or true.

name: php_get_id_numeric_juggle
reason: PHP's "1abc" == 1 numeric-string coercion lets a crafted id bypass the check.

name: php_post_role_boolean_juggle
reason: true == any non-empty string in PHP, so any non-empty role value grants access.

name: php_post_token_null_juggle
reason: NULL-coercion via == lets an unexpected token value skip validation entirely.

name: strcmp_eq_zero_loose_request
reason: strcmp() returns NULL on array input; NULL == 0 is TRUE, bypassing the PIN check.

name: strcmp_eq_zero_generic_vars
reason: strcmp(...) == 0 is vulnerable regardless of variable naming; array input yields NULL == 0.

name: strcmp_ne_zero_loose
reason: If strcmp() returns NULL (array input), NULL != 0 is FALSE, so deny_access() is skipped.

name: bang_strcmp_bare
reason: !strcmp(...) treats a NULL (array-input) return as truthy, granting a false match.

name: bang_strcmp_spaced
reason: Whitespace between ! and strcmp( is still the bare-negated strcmp() bypass.

name: in_array_get_non_strict
reason: in_array() without strict mode loosely compares, letting a magic-hash-shaped string match.

name: in_array_post_non_strict
reason: Missing strict third argument means role comparison uses loose == semantics.

name: in_array_cookie_non_strict
reason: A cookie-sourced needle checked with non-strict in_array() is loosely compared.

name: md5_loose_eq
reason: md5(...) == is vulnerable to "0e..." magic-hash collisions.

name: sha1_loose_eq
reason: sha1(...) == is vulnerable to "0e..." magic-hash collisions the same way as md5.

name: md5_reversed_loose_eq
reason: The magic-hash collision applies regardless of operand order in the == comparison.

name: sha1_reversed_loose_ne
reason: A loose != against a sha1() result is exploitable the same way as a loose ==.

name: two_hash_vars_loose_eq
reason: Two hash-looking values compared with loose == still permit a magic-hash collision.

name: two_hash_vars_loose_ne
reason: Loose != between two hash values is exploitable the same way as loose ==.

name: strict_eq_post
reason: === requires identical type and value; PHP performs no coercion, so no bypass is possible.

name: strict_ne_get
reason: !== is the strict not-identical operator and does not type-juggle.

name: strcmp_strict_eq_zero
reason: === 0 distinguishes strcmp()'s integer 0 return from a NULL failure return.

name: strcmp_strict_ne_zero
reason: !== 0 correctly treats a NULL return as not-identical-to-zero, so deny_access() still runs.

name: in_array_strict_third_arg
reason: The strict third argument `true` forces type-and-value comparison, no loose bypass.

name: hash_equals_clean
reason: hash_equals() is timing-safe and never performs a loose == comparison.

name: md5_strict_eq
reason: === requires an exact string match, so a "0e..." magic-hash collision cannot forge a match.

name: sha1_strict_eq
reason: === requires an exact string match, so a "0e..." magic-hash collision cannot forge a match.

name: two_hash_vars_strict_eq
reason: Two hash-looking values compared with === cannot be forged by a magic-hash collision.

name: numeric_constants_loose_eq_no_input
reason: No PHP request-input superglobal is present, so there is no attacker-controlled operand.

name: string_constants_loose_eq_no_input
reason: Comparing a local variable to a fixed string literal with no request input is not attacker-influenced.

name: bang_operator_unrelated
reason: ! prefixes empty(), not strcmp(); this is not the bare-negated strcmp() bypass.

name: single_hash_var_no_comparison
reason: A single hash-named variable in an assignment (not a comparison) cannot trigger the two-hash loose-compare check, and there is no md5()/sha1() call site.

name: prose_comment_mentions_concept
input: // Historical note: this file used to rely on PHP loose comparison for auth.
reason: Bare prose describing the vulnerability class, with no request-input token or comparison operator present, must not be flagged.

name: password_verify_clean
reason: password_verify() is a single function call with no ==/!= operator on the line.

name: assignment_not_comparison
reason: A single = assignment is not a comparison; $_POST co-occurring with a lone = must not be flagged.
